questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with South Sudan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture South Sudan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the South Sudan article.

questions.proof: The country is bordered by Ethiopia to the east; Kenya to the southeast; Uganda to the south; the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the southwest; the Central African Republic to the west; and the Republic of Sudan to the north.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: South Sudan about 644,329 square kilometres; Malawi about 118,484 square kilometres; Eritrea about 117,600 square kilometres; Burundi about 27,834 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Juba?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of South Sudan is Juba.

questions.prompt: What money is used in South Sudan?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in South Sudan is the South Sudanese pound.

questions.prompt: Which continent is South Sudan in?

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find South Sudan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find South Sudan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
